primary_claim: Thought Anchors-style resampling and causal-masking techniques, originally validated on math reasoning, transfer meaningfully to legal reasoning in R1-Distill-Llama models: thought anchors exist but are dominated by fact-retrieval sentences rather than planning, attention weight only weakly correlates with causal (resampling) importance (Pearson r=0.23), and attention probes can predict the model's evolving judgment-leaning with up to 95% sign-match accuracy on held-out legal cases.

effect.metric: attention-vs-resampling-importance correlation; probe sign-match accuracy on held-out cases
effect.value: Pearson r=0.23 (attention vs. causal/resampling importance); attention probes achieve up to 95% sign-match accuracy on held-out legal cases, 85% even with only 10% of trace used for training (frac=0.1)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Unlike the original Thought Anchors paper (math reasoning), where thought anchors were planning/uncertainty-management sentences, in legal reasoning thought anchors are primarily fact-retrieval sentences

Unlike Thought Anchors' reported high correlation between resampling importance and causal-masking importance, this work found little qualitative overlap between different importance metrics (confounded by using different model scales for each technique)
stated_future_work: Implement a more targeted attention analysis focusing on syntactically/semantically salient tokens instead of averaging over full sentences
Test on a larger set of cases and models to clarify whether the weak attention-causal correlation is genuine or a power issue
Investigate whether specific circuits (e.g. induction heads) explain long-range causal dependencies between sentences
Simultaneously mask restatements of facts to uncover how the model builds novel inferences
Run formal correlation analyses between importance metrics using unified model infrastructure across techniques
limitations_stated: Different model scales were used for different techniques (8B for masking vs. 70B for resampling), limiting cross-technique comparison
Long-range sentence dependencies may be artifacts of token overlap / induction heads rather than genuine reasoning
Probes trained on legal cases gave mixed to poor results when tested on other judgment domains
quote: Thought anchors exist in legal reasoning but center on fact retrieval rather than planning.
